i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid initializePathMatrix(std::vector<unsigned int>& path, const size_t numNodes) {\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            path[idx2(i, j, numNodes)] = j;\n            path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = i;\n        }\n        path[idx2(j, j, numNodes)] = j;\n    }\n}\n\n// One Floyd-Warshall relaxation step for intermediate node k, applied to every (i, j) pair.\n// Row k and column k are not modified during the step (dist[k][k] == 0), so each cell\n// reads only values that no other thread writes in this step and all cells can run in parallel.\n__global__ void floydWarshallStep(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist,\n                                  unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n                                  const size_t numNodes,\n                                  const size_t k) {\n    const size_t j = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t i = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (i >= numNodes || j >= numNodes) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n    const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n    const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n\n    const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n\n    if (newDist < distIJ) {\n        dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = newDist;\n        path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n    }\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    if (numNodes == 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const size_t bytes = numNodes * numNodes * sizeof(unsigned int);\n\n    unsigned int* dDist = nullptr;\n    unsigned int* dPath = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dDist, bytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dPath, bytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dDist, dist.data(), bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dPath, path.data(), bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    // Each step k depends on the result of step k-1, so the steps are launched in order on\n    // one stream. Within a step, all n*n cells are processed in parallel by the grid.\n    const dim3 block(32, 8);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned int>((numNodes + block.x - 1) / block.x),\n                    static_cast<unsigned int>((numNodes + block.y - 1) / block.y));\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        floydWarshallStep<<<grid, block>>>(dDist, dPath, numNodes, k);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    // Blocking copies wait for all queued kernels to finish.\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dist.data(), dDist, bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(path.data(), dPath, bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dDist));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dPath));\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Basic sanity checks\n    \n    // 1. {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++j) {\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n                \n                // triangle inequality violated at [%zu,%zu,%zu]\\n\", \n                               i, j, k);\n                        return false;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of   \n    // Allocate matrices\n    std::vector<unsigned int> dist(numNodes * numNodes);\n    std::vector<unsigned int> path(numNodes * numNodes);\n    \n    // Initialize\n    printf(\"Initializing {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfyvghGH7TNj9vUsUKFqQ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Floyd-Warshall benchmark now runs entirely on the GPU. It is compiled as CUDA, and it reproduces the original program's output exactly on every size I tested.\n\n**Results on the RTX 3090 (CUDA 12.0)**\n\n| n | Original CPU | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512 (default) | 165 ms | 4 ms |\n| 1000 | 1143 ms | 15 ms |\n| 2048 | 9384 ms | 88 ms |\n\n**Correctness**\n- The `DistanceMatrix` hashes match the original for n = 1, 2, 7, 64, 100, 512, 1000 and 2048, and validation passes.\n- The `path` matrix is not printed, so I checked it separately in scratch copies that print a hash of it. It is bit-identical to the original for every size tested.\n\n**What changed**\n- `floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp`: the CPU triple loop is replaced by a `floydWarshallStep` kernel, which handles one `(i, j)` cell per thread, and a `floydWarshall` wrapper with the same signature. The wrapper copies the matrices to the device, runs one launch per intermediate node `k` in order, and copies both matrices back. Host initialization and validation are unchanged. The output format is unchanged.\n- `floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`: the project now enables CUDA. The `.cpp` is compiled as CUDA via `LANGUAGE CUDA`, the target name is still `floydwarshall`, and `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` is `native`. It now requires CMake 3.24 or newer.\n- No new files were created. The `build/` directory I used during testing has been removed.\n\n**Choices you may want to review**\n- **Exact step order, not blocked FW.** Each `k` is a separate launch. Blocked or tiled Floyd-Warshall would be faster at large n. However, it changes the order of updates, which can change which `k` gets recorded in `path`, even when the distances are the same. I kept the exact order to preserve equivalence.\n- **Timing scope.** \"Computation time\" covers the host-to-device copy, the kernels and the device-to-host copy. It excludes CUDA context creation, which is forced before the timer starts. Without that, the first call costs about 2 s.\n- **Integer milliseconds.** The `%ld ms` output format is kept. At n=512 it resolves only to whole milliseconds, so the GOPS figure is coarse.\n- **Large n is memory-bound.** At n=4096 it takes about 0.5 s, because each step streams the full matrix from DRAM.\n- **Things I tried and dropped.** A CUDA graph over the step launches was slower (9 ms vs 4 ms at n=512). Other block shapes made no meaningful difference, so I kept 32×8.\n\nI did not commit anything, since you didn't ask for a commit and this directory is not a git repository."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1021,"cache_read_input_tokens":45617,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1021},"output_tokens":9,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d062fcaf-a0ee-4596-af98-cc41d262666a","uuid":"fc0dedf1-f579-4dee-a29d-6f7753e84609","timestamp":"2026-10-13T08:32:47.301Z","request_id":"req_011CfyvggxRbyU1QxzNEeSev"}
